notes:
Summary: Mid-market multi-tenant SaaS (AgentFlow) building hosted agent product for customer support automation. Evaluating Redwood Hosted API as quick path + Dedicated for production. Key emphasis on streaming latency SLOs, tool calling reliability, and per-tenant quotas/quotas enforcement.

Recent timeline / highlights:
- 2025-11-02: initial inbound, product demo request. AE: Ellen. SE intro: Ravi.
- 2026-01-12: discovery call (ff_20260220_amberleaf_intro) — discussed architecture: multi-tenant router, single inference layer, per-tenant billing.
- 2026-02-06: Hosted API demo: streaming + function/tool calling demo (good UX, hit 3rd-party tool limits).
- 2026-02-18: POC kickoff (hosted) — baseline integration completed, ingesting tenant metadata, initial token accounting.
- 2026-02-24: POC stress test (ff_20260224_poc_retrospective): functional correctness OK, but observed 90th/95th pct tail latency spikes during simulated burst (multi-tenant traffic). SE notes: batching params and KV cache warmup need tuning.
- 2026-03-01: Security questionnaire submitted (see Drive doc). Legal requested data residency language + audit log retention.
- 2026-03-05: Pricing follow-up; Amberleaf ops asks about guaranteed tail-latency SLA and reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated.

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- CTO: "We need median <40ms and 95th <200ms for streaming events across tenants; streaming must resume gracefully if client reconnects."
- Head of Product: "Per-tenant soft/hard quotas + burst tokens are critical — we bill tenants by usage and need strict enforcement and accurate accounting."

Technical requirements (customer stated):
- Workload: multi-tenant conversational agents (human+tool flows), average session length 1.2k tokens, heavy tool-calling (search, CRM lookup).
- Latency targets: median token latency ~30-50ms, 95th percentile under 200ms at expected peak TPS (~350 concurrent sessions).
- Throughput: peaks ~250K tokens/min during campaigns; need autoscale + predictable tail.
- Reliability: streaming stability (resume/rewind on reconnect; dedupe), KV cache per-tenant separation, fallbacks to smaller model variants without changing API surface.
- Operational: per-tenant quotas, burst handling, per-tenant billing hooks, token-level cost visibility.
- Security/compliance: Okta SSO, audit logs retention 1y, optional regional data residency (EU), KMS integration for customer keys.

POC outcomes so far:
- Hosted API: fast time-to-value; integration complete; function calling works for CRM lookups.
- Performance: functional correct but tail latency issues under burst; Redwood SE recommended testing Dedicated with reserved GPU pool and specific batching/quantization profile.
- Observability: Amberleaf liked Console traces and per-route latency breakdown; asked for per-tenant views.

Pricing / commercial notes:
- Amberleaf prefers a path: start hosted (inc. credits) for beta -> convert to Dedicated reserved capacity for production if latency SLOs met.
- Finance: wants 12-mo commit pricing for Dedicated if 95th latency SLA can be contractually guaranteed.
- Estimated ARR if convert: $60k-$150k / year depending on reserved capacity tier.

Open questions / blockers to close:
- Can Redwood guarantee 95th-tail latency for streaming at scale (contract language)?
- Exact per-tenant quota semantics (soft vs hard cap, throttling behavior, webhook on throttle).
- Streaming resume behaviour: how are partial responses retransmitted / deduped?
- Pricing for multi-tenant per-tenant rate limits + reserved capacity with burst.
- Legal: data residency clause and KMS/HSM integration details.

Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-10: SE deep-dive to run dedicated-config perf sim for Amberleaf workload (Ravi + Amberleaf infra).
- Provide a sample Dedicated sizing + cost estimate and SLA language by 2026-03-13.
- Align on test plan for streaming stability (reconnect, resume, duplicate detection) and per-tenant quota behaviour.

Stubs/links: Drive pricing deck (see linked_drive_docs), Jira RD-2345 ticket for tail-latency logs, Gmail threads for Okta mapping.

Notes intake style: fragmented bullets, internal ops shorthand mixed with customer quotes.
